---
title: "R and RStudio"
---

Install R, RStudio Desktop, and a practical user-level package set for data analysis, teaching, and research.

```sh
ansible-playbook -i inventory -K playbooks/lab-stack.yml --tags rstudio
```

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| R | Statistical computing language and development files for compiling packages. |
| RStudio Desktop | Local open-source IDE for interactive R work. |
| Analysis packages | tidyverse, tidymodels, janitor, skimr, here, writexl, and openxlsx. |
| Authoring and development packages | knitr, rmarkdown, quarto, renv, testthat, and languageserver. |

## Launch RStudio

Open **RStudio** from the desktop application menu, or launch it from a terminal:

```sh
rstudio
```

Packages managed by this role are installed in `~/R/library`, so they are owned by the workstation user rather than root.

Use `renv` within individual projects to record and restore project-specific package versions. The shared user library is a practical starting set, not a replacement for a reproducible project environment.

[Rocker](https://rocker-project.org/) images remain available through Docker when a project requires container-level reproducibility. Containers are optional and are not required for normal local RStudio use.

## Troubleshoot package installation

Fedora compiles CRAN packages from source. The role installs the required system
development libraries and automatically retries transient download failures. The
first package installation can therefore take several minutes.

If the role reports a package lock, close R and RStudio before rerunning it. A
rerun is safe: the role skips configured top-level packages that are already
installed and retries only those still missing.

::: {.callout-check}
**✅ Check**

```sh
R --version
rstudio --version
Rscript -e 'library(tidyverse); library(tidymodels); sessionInfo()'
```
:::
